history.dynasty: Namgyal dynasty (Sikkimese monarchy) as patrons; rebuilt by the Karma Kagyu lineage under the 16th Gyalwa Karmapa
history.period: Original foundation: CONFLICT - 16th century under the 9th Karmapa Wangchuk Dorje (Tibetan Buddhist Encyclopedia, travel sources) vs mid-18th century under the 12th Karmapa Changchub Dorje (Wikipedia); present complex built 1962-66 and inaugurated at Losar 1966 (Wikipedia; sikkimeccl says founded 1962)
history.summary: THIS IS A BUDDHIST MONASTERY (KARMA KAGYU TIBETAN BUDDHISM) - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE; keep-or-drop decision needed. Rumtek Monastery, also called the Dharma Chakra Centre, is the seat-in-exile of the Gyalwang Karmapa, the spiritual head of the Karma Kagyu lineage, and the International Headquarters of the Kagyupa sect. The original monastery (attributed to either the 9th Karmapa Wangchuk Dorje in the 16th century or the 12th Karmapa Changchub Dorje in the mid-18th century - sources conflict) had fallen into ruins when the 16th Karmapa, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924-1981), fled Tibet in 1959 with ~160 monks carrying the lineage's most sacred treasures and relics. Chogyal Sir Tashi Namgyal offered him asylum and 74 acres at Rumtek, where the Karmapa chose the ruined monastery site; construction of the new complex (modelled on Tsurphu, the Karmapas' Tibetan seat) took about four years and the sacred items brought from Tsurphu were installed. On Losar 1966 he formally inaugurated 'The Dharmachakra Centre, a place of erudition and spiritual accomplishment, the seat of the glorious Karmapa'. The complex includes the Golden Stupa with the 16th Karmapa's relics (he died 5 Nov 1981 and was cremated here 20 Dec 1981), his preserved holy crown (said to be woven by the dakinis), the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute for Higher Buddhist Studies (sheda), and a circumambulation stupa walkway; the gonpa is reported to house 243 monks and 186 novice monks (verify). The monastery is also the focal point of the sectarian 17th-Karmapa controversy within the Karma Kagyu school.

name: Rumtek Monastery (Dharma Chakra Centre)
town_description: Rumtek is a hilltop settlement about 24 km from Gangtok in Gangtok district (East Sikkim), at ~1,500 m altitude. It lies on the opposite flank of the valley from the Sikkimese capital - monastery rooftops look straight across at Gangtok - with streams running below, mountains behind and an open outlook, the auspicious qualities for which the site was chosen. The area is dominated by the monastery complex, the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, and monastic quarters.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Karma Kagyu) - NOT a Hindu temple

travel.airport: Nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB), approx. 124-160 km (verify); Pakyong Airport is closer but has limited flights.
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approx. 125-150 km (verify).
travel.road: About 24 km from Gangtok; vehicles generally stop at the lower security gate, then a ~10-minute uphill paved walk to the monastery courtyard (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: March to June or September to November for mild, clear weather; visit at Losar (Tibetan New Year) for ceremonies.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT: the monastery's own site lists 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily; one travel aggregator lists 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM (verify before visiting). Entry ticket around Rs. 10 reported (verify). Photography inside the shrine hall is restricted (verify).
